To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the survival and mRNA levels in the magnocellular neurone (MCN) of the hypothalamus are dependent on the presence of the neurotrophic factor, ciliary neurotropic factor (CNTF).

CNTF is a survival factor for the vasopressing magnocellular neurons in vitro and the presence of CTF at the outset is required to rescue vasopressing MCNs from axotomy‐induced apoptosis, but once the MCNs survive, they do not require the presence of CTRF for their continued survival.

the presence of ciliary neurotrohic factor (CNTF; 10 ng/ml) in the culture medium for the first 10 days of a 14‐day in vitro culture period is required to produce a significant increase in the survival and vasopressi mRNA expression of magnocellular neurone in the hypothalamic supraoptic nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cell survival in the hypothalamo‐neurohypophysis system.
the long‐term survival and maintenance of vasopressine neurones in the hypothalamic organ culture.
elucidating the mechanisms of action of CNTF on MCNs and with determining how CNTF can be used to maintain MCN survival in hypothalamic organotypical cultures.

CNTF can increase the survival of both vasopressin‐MCNs and oxytocin‐neurones in the SON in vitro, and that these effects are maximal when CNTF is present in the media from the onset of the culture and for a period of 10 days.

CNTF is effective in increasing the survival of vasotocin MCNs in organotypic cultures of the hypothalami, but only if it is present at the outset of the culture period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CNTFs are able to rescue the axotomized vasopressin‐ and oxytocin‐neurones in the SON from the initial period of apoptosis, but the CNTF does not rescue the neurones from the secondary period of apoptosis.
CNTF can rescue vasopressing MCNs from apoptosis, and that this effect requires the presence of CTF for the first 7–10 days in culture.
the CNTFs are a family of proteins that have been shown to be neuroprotective in a variety of cell types.

CNTF treatment is an effective means of rescuing the MCNs in vitro and can be used to examine the long‐term effects of various experimental manipulations in the MCNs.
